events.title: Jesus' Genealogy
events.description: Matthew introduces his Gospel with Jesus' genealogy from Abraham through David to Joseph, Mary's husband. The genealogy is arranged in three groups of fourteen generations and shows that Jesus is the promised Messiah of David's line.

events.title: The Birth of Jesus
events.description: Mary is engaged to Joseph but has become pregnant by the Holy Spirit. An angel appears to Joseph in a dream and tells him that the child is from God, and that he should name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins. Joseph takes Mary as his wife.

events.title: The Magi from the East
events.description: Magi from the East come to Jerusalem and ask about the newborn king of the Jews. They have seen his star and wish to worship him. The star leads them to Bethlehem where they find the child, fall down and worship him, and give gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh.

events.title: The Flight to Egypt
events.description: An angel warns Joseph in a dream that Herod intends to kill the child. Joseph flees with Mary and Jesus to Egypt, where they stay until Herod dies. Herod orders the killing of all male children under two years old in Bethlehem, but the holy family is already safe.

events.title: The Baptism of Jesus
events.description: Jesus comes from Galilee to the Jordan to be baptized by John. As he rises out of the water, the heavens open, and God's Spirit descends upon him like a dove. A voice from heaven says: "This is my Son, the beloved. In him I am well pleased."

events.title: The Temptation in the Wilderness
events.description: The Spirit leads Jesus into the wilderness where he fasts for forty days and forty nights. The devil tempts him three times: with bread, by telling him to throw himself down from the temple, and with the kingdoms of the world. Jesus rejects each temptation with God's word.

events.title: The Ministry in Galilee Begins
events.description: After John is imprisoned, Jesus withdraws to Galilee and settles in Capernaum. He begins to preach: "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near!" He calls his first disciples: Simon Peter, Andrew, James, and John.

events.title: The Sermon on the Mount
events.description: Jesus goes up on a mountain and teaches the crowds and his disciples. He speaks about the Beatitudes, about being the salt of the earth and the light of the world, about the law, prayer, fasting, and trust in God. The sermon concludes with the parable of the two houses.

events.title: Healings and Miracles
events.description: Jesus heals a leper, an officer's servant in Capernaum, Peter's mother-in-law, and many other sick people. He calms the storm on the sea and drives out evil spirits. The crowds are filled with awe at his power and authority.

events.title: Matthew is Called
events.description: Jesus sees the tax collector Matthew sitting at the tax booth and says to him: "Follow me!" Matthew gets up immediately and follows him. Jesus eats a meal in his house with many tax collectors and sinners, which causes offense among the Pharisees.

events.title: The Twelve Apostles are Sent Out
events.description: Jesus calls the twelve disciples to himself and gives them authority to drive out unclean spirits and heal every kind of disease. He sends them out to the lost sheep of Israel with the message that the kingdom of heaven has come near, and gives them detailed instructions for their mission.

events.title: John's Question from Prison
events.description: John the Baptist sends his disciples from prison to ask Jesus: "Are you the one who is to come, or shall we look for another?" Jesus answers by pointing to his works: the blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, and the dead are raised.

events.title: The Parable of the Sower
events.description: Jesus tells the parable of a sower who planted seed that fell on four types of soil: along the path, on rocky ground, among thorns, and in good soil. He explains that the parable is about how people receive God's word in different ways.

events.title: The Feeding of the Five Thousand
events.description: Jesus withdraws to a lonely place, but a large crowd follows him. In the evening he feeds more than five thousand people with only five loaves and two fish. Afterwards, the disciples gather twelve full baskets of what is left over.

events.title: Jesus Walks on Water
events.description: After the feeding, Jesus sends the disciples out onto the sea while he goes up on a mountain to pray. In the fourth watch of the night, he comes walking toward them on the water. Peter tries to walk to him but sinks when he sees the wind and becomes afraid.

events.title: Peter Confesses Jesus as the Messiah
events.description: At Caesarea Philippi, Jesus asks his disciples who people say he is. Peter answers: "You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God." Jesus says that Peter is the rock on which he will build his church and gives him the keys to the kingdom of heaven.

events.title: The Transfiguration on the Mountain
events.description: Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a high mountain. There he is transformed before their eyes: his face shines like the sun and his clothes become white as light. Moses and Elijah appear and speak with him, and a voice from the cloud says: "This is my Son, the beloved."

events.title: The Entry into Jerusalem
events.description: Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a donkey, just as the prophet Zechariah had foretold. The crowds lay cloaks and palm branches on the road and shout: "Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!" The whole city is stirred.

events.title: The Cleansing of the Temple
events.description: Jesus enters the temple and drives out all who are buying and selling there. He overturns the tables of the money changers and the benches of those selling doves. He says: "My house shall be called a house of prayer, but you make it a den of robbers."

events.title: The Eschatological Discourse
events.description: On the Mount of Olives, the disciples ask about the sign of Jesus' return and the end of the world. Jesus speaks of false prophets, wars, persecutions, and great tribulations. He urges watchfulness through the parables of the ten virgins and the talents, and describes the final judgment.

events.title: The Last Supper
events.description: Jesus celebrates the Passover meal with the twelve disciples. During the meal, he institutes the Lord's Supper: he breaks bread and says "this is my body", and gives them the cup saying "this is my blood, the blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins".

events.title: Gethsemane
events.description: Jesus takes Peter, James, and John to the garden of Gethsemane to pray. He is filled with anguish and sorrow and prays: "My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me! Yet not as I will, but as you will." The disciples fall asleep three times while he prays.

events.title: The Arrest
events.description: Judas arrives with a large crowd armed with swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests and elders of the people. He betrays Jesus with a kiss. Peter cuts off the ear of the high priest's servant, but Jesus tells him to put his sword back in its place, saying he could ask his Father for twelve legions of angels.

events.title: The Trial Before the Council
events.description: Jesus is brought before the high priest Caiaphas where the whole council has gathered. False witnesses accuse him, but Jesus remains silent. When the high priest asks if he is the Messiah, the Son of God, Jesus answers affirmatively. The council condemns him to death for blasphemy.

events.title: Peter's Denial
events.description: While Jesus is being questioned inside, Peter sits outside in the courtyard. Three times he is recognized as one of Jesus' followers, and three times he denies it. When the rooster crows, Peter remembers Jesus' words and goes out and weeps bitterly.

events.title: The Crucifixion
events.description: Jesus is taken to Golgotha and crucified between two criminals. From the sixth hour until the ninth hour, darkness covers the whole land. Jesus cries out: "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?" and gives up his spirit. The curtain in the temple is torn in two, the earth shakes, and rocks split.

events.title: The Resurrection
events.description: Early on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary come to the tomb. The earth shakes, and an angel descends from heaven, rolling away the stone. The angel says: "He is not here; he has risen!" Jesus himself meets the women on the way and greets them.

events.title: The Great Commission
events.description: The eleven disciples go to the mountain in Galilee where Jesus had told them to meet him. Jesus steps forward and says: "All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. Go therefore and make disciples of all nations." He promises to be with them every day until the end of the age.
